Test Leiden clustering resolutions on a nearest-neighbour graph

Source: R/test_resolution.R
test_resolution.Rd

Runs Leiden community detection across a range of resolution values and returns a summary table of clustering metrics for each resolution. Use this function to select an appropriate resolution before running create_communities.

Usage

test_resolution(
  sce,
  graph.name = "RNA_snn",
  resolutions = c(0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20),
  min_cells = 5
)

Arguments

sce

A SingleCellExperiment object. The object must contain a pre-computed nearest-neighbour graph stored in metadata(sce)$graphs under the name given by graph.name. See the Graph preparation section below for how to build and store the graph.

graph.name

A character string giving the name of the graph to retrieve from metadata(sce)$graphs. Defaults to "RNA_snn".

resolutions

A numeric vector of resolution values to test. Higher values produce more, smaller communities. Defaults to c(0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 20).

min_cells

A positive integer that defines the minimum community size. Communities with fewer than this many cells are considered too small and each of the consistuent cells are reassigned to the valid community occupied by the majority of the cell's nearest neighbours/ Defaults to 5.

Value

A data.frame with one row per tested resolution and the following columns:

resolution

The resolution value tested.

n_communities

Number of communities after reassignment of small clusters.

mean_cells_per_community

Mean community size.

sd_cells_per_community

Standard deviation of community sizes.

median_cells_per_community

Median community size.

min_cells_per_community

Smallest community size.

max_cells_per_community

Largest community size.

modularity

Graph modularity of the partition.

Resolutions at which all communities fall below min_cells are skipped with a warning and will not appear in the output.

Details

Graph preparation:

This function does not build the nearest-neighbour graph itself. The graph must be computed and stored in metadata(sce)$graphs before calling this function. Two workflows are supported:

1. From scratch with scran:


library(scran)

# Build a shared nearest-neighbour graph on the PCA embedding
g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)

# Store it under the name this function will look for
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

2. From an existing Seurat object:


library(Seurat)

# Convert to SCE first
sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_obj)

# Extract the adjacency matrix from the Seurat object, convert to igraph,
# and store in the SCE metadata
g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  seurat_obj@graphs[["RNA_snn"]],
  mode     = "max",
  weighted = TRUE
)
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

The value passed to graph.name must match the key used when storing the graph in metadata(sce)$graphs.

See also

create_communities to assign cells to communities once a resolution has been chosen

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(scran)

# Build and store the graph
g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

# Test a range of resolutions
res_results <- test_resolution(sce, resolutions = c(0.5, 1, 2.5, 5))
print(res_results)
} # }
